question.prompt: Abby, Bridget, and four of their classmates will be seated in two rows of three for a group picture, as shown. \[\begin{array}{ccc} \text{\text{X}}&\text{X}&\text{X} \\ \text{X}&\text{X}&\text{X} \end{array}\] If the seating positions are assigned randomly, what is the probability that Abby and Bridget are adjacent to each other in the same row or the same column?

solutions.explanation:
Count the pair of seats occupied by Abby and Bridget. Every unordered pair of seats is equally likely: either girl can occupy either seat, and the other four classmates can fill the remaining seats in the same number of ways.

There are \(6\cdot5/2=15\) seat pairs. We divide by \(2\) because choosing the two seats in the opposite order gives the same pair.

In each row of three seats, there are two adjacent pairs, for \(4\) horizontal pairs altogether. There is also one vertical pair in each of the \(3\) columns. Thus there are \(4+3=7\) favorable pairs, and the probability is

\[
\boxed{\frac7{15}},
\]

choice \(\boxed{\text{C}}\). Counting pairs of positions removes the irrelevant arrangements of the other classmates.
solutions.title: Count equally likely unordered seat pairs
